BiblicalUsage: liparós means dainty, and the verse where it stands does the talking. In Revelation 18:14, "and all things which were dainty and goodly are departed from thee".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Babylon's dainty fruits are the picture of luxury that does not last — all things dainty and goodly departed, and they shall be found no more.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
